 Bengaluru  J U D G M E N T That, the plaintiff has filed this suit for declaration to declare that (a) She is absolute owner in possession of suit 'A' schedule property,

The plaintiff has also sought for consequential relief of perpetual injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with possession and enjoyment of suit 'A' property by the plaintiff.

a.

The plaintiff has pleaded that she is the absolute owner in lawful possession &

The plaintiff further averred that as per re- grant order made by Assistant Commissioner, the Tahasildar had put them in actual possession of their respective lands and M.R.NO.4/1982-83 has been effected.

Katha and other revenue records have been transferred in favour of the Chikkathimma,
Muniraju and Munirama.

The plaintiff submits that for formation of National Highway No.7 an area of 00-03-00 each belonging to Chikkathimma, Munirama and Muniraju have been acquired by Government and after acquisition of land 00-13-00 was retained by Chikkathimma S/o Thimma, 00-12-00 was retained by Munirama S/o Thimma and 00-12-00 was retained by Muniraju S/o Thimma.

It is further submitted by the plaintiff that Munirama S/o Thimma and Muniraju S/o Thimma have jointly sold remaining land belonging to them i.e., 12 guntas each in favour of one K. Bhaskar through a registered Sale Deed dated 07.01.1994.

Chikkathimma, Muniraju and Munirama have jointly drawn .56,463/- vide cheque bearing No.F74417 dated 10.04.1995 towards the compensation amount in respect of the land acquired by National Highway authority.

It is further submitted by the plaintiff that Munirama, Muniraju have requested the Assistant Commissioner Bengaluru to enter their names in respect of land bearing Sy.No.5/1 to the extent of 3 guntas each by suppressing the fact of acquisition of land for formation of National Highway No.7.

It is submitted by the plaintiff that Tahasildar Bengaluru South has also ordered to enter name of defendant No.1 to 7 area 00-03-00 in new Sy.No.5/3 vide M.R.NO.8/09-10.

The Assistant Commissioner has granted interim order was stay.

The plaintiff contended that the defendants in collusion with revenue authorities have created revenue records in their favour and are trying to alienate the suit schedule properties for wrongful gain.
Plaintiff submits that defendants have no manner of right, title or interest over suit 'B' and 'C' schedule properties.
Plaintiff further submits that she is the absolute owner of 'A' schedule property and she is in lawful possession & enjoyment of suit property.

The defendant No.1 to 11 have denied that plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession of suit 'A'

It is submitted by the defendant No.1 to 11 that Chikkathimma-husband of plaintiff, Munirama father of defendant No.2 to 7 and Muniraju husband of defendant No.8 and father of defendant No.9 to 11 were brothers.

The defendant NO.1 to 11 submit that S.L.A.O vide award dated 30.04.1994 passed in LAQ:BLR.5/90-91 has awarded an amount of .56,463/- which is received by Chikkathimma on 10.11.1995.

It is further submitted by defendant No.1 to 11 that remaining 00-06-00 of land owned by husband of the plaintiff in Sy.No.5/1 again 1  gunta additional land was acquired by NH-7 and compensation is awarded as per LAQ/BLR/3/96-97 to the tune of .15,316/-.

It is further contended by defendant No.1 to 11 that though 11  guntas of land out of 00-16-00 in Sy.No.5/1 was acquired by National Highway Authority & there was only 4  guntas of land remaining without disclosing the same, the husband of the plaintiff and her sons have got deleted name of NH-7 from revenue records and taking disadvantage, they have executed sale agreement in respect of entire 00-16-00 in favour of one K. The defendant No.1 to 11 have contended that under sale agreement dated 29.06.1995 the husband of the plaintiff has received .3,00,000/- and failed to execute the Sale Deed in favour of K. Gajendra agreement holder.

Accordingly, O.S.No.5100 of 1998 came to be filed before City Civil Court Bengaluru for specific performance of the contract directing the husband of the plaintiff and her sons to execute the registered Sale Deed.

Being dissatisfied by the judgment & decree passed in O.S.No.5100 of 1998 Gajendra preferred an appeal before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at RFA.No.543 of 2005, which came to be allowed directing the husband of the plaintiff and her sons to execute the Sale Deed vide judgment & order dated 27.09.2007.

The defendant No.1 to 11 submit that plaintiff by suppressing the sale of land has filed this suit questioning the ownership of defendants in suit 'B' and 'C'

4) a) The defendant No.12 has been subsequently impleaded in this suit.
The defendant No.12 has filed separate written statement.

In the written statement defendant No.12 has contended that suit is barred by limitation, not maintainable for want of seeking possession, for non-payment of proper court fees, non-joinder of necessary parties is liable to be dismissed.
The defendant No.12 contended that Chikkathimma, Munirama and Muniraju are brothers and they have been granted lands in Sy.No.5/1 of Singasandra Village.
It is submitted by defendant No.12 that Chikkathimma was granted 00-16-00 of land, Muniraju and Munirama were granted 00-15-00 each in Sy.No.5/1.

The defendant No.12 contended that Munirama and Muniraju sold properties that fell to their shares in Sy.No.5/1 measuring 24 guntas as per Sale Deed dated 07.01.1994 to one K. Bhaskar and retained 00-03-00 each.

It is submitted by defendant No.12 that K. Bhaskar was in possession as owner of the property till 2006 and on 19.04.2006 defendant No.12 purchased 14 guntas of land out of 24 guntas sold in favour of K.
Bhaskar vide registered Sale Deed.
The defendant No.12 contended that he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of 00-12-00 of land sold as per Sale Deed dated 19.04.2006 and he has acquired right, title and interest over the same.

b) It is submitted by defendant No.12 that Chikkathimma and his children suppressing the fact of acquisition of 11.5 guntas of land by National Highway Authority entered into an Agreement of sale dated 29.06.1995 with one K. Gajendra by receiving .3,00,000/-.

Chikkathimma and his children have failed to comply with the terms & conditions of agreement of sale and accordingly, K.
Ganjendra filed O.S.No.5100 of 1998 seeking specific performance of the contract.

The defendant No.12 contended that as per judgment passed in RFA.No.543 of 2005 Gajendra is entitled for specific performance of the contract and Chikkathimma and his children were directed to execute the Sale Deed in respect of their land.
Children of Chikkathimma have preferred Special Leave Petition which came to be dismissed.
It is submitted by the defendant No.12 that Gajendra has got right to seek execution of judgment & decree in respect of remaining land of 4.5 guntas in Sy.No.5/1.

It is further submitted by defendant No.12 that certain disputes arose between Muniraju &
Munirama on the one hand and Chikkathimma's family on the other hand in respect of residual property that they had retained with them, apart from 24 guntas conveyed to K. Bhaskar.

It is submitted by defendant No.12 that 11.5 guntas of land was acquired by NHAI for establishment of highways, the dispute that arose amongst family members whether 11.5 guntas was acquired from the portion of Chikkathimma or Chikkathimma's land was limited to 4.5 guntas only.

This dispute led to the proceedings before Assistant Commissioner Bengaluru which culminated in an order dated 27.06.2012 which clearly held that entire portion of 11.5 guntas acquired by NHAI was acquired from the lands belonging to Chikkathimmaiah and consequently Muniraju & Munirama retained 3 guntas each.

It is important to mention here that Chikkathimma and his legal heirs have also received compensation awarded in respect of their property acquired by NHAI to the extent of Hanumakka vs Muniyamma on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114126643/
9 11.5 guntas in Sy.No.5/1.

Therefore, the defendant No.12 contended that in pursuance of order of Assistant Commissioner defendant NO.12 has purchased remaining 00-6-00 of land from family members of Muniraju and Munirama vide Sale Deed dated 24.09.2011. 00-06-00 of land purchased
were entered in the name of defendant No.12 and he is in possession and enjoyment of the property.

It is submitted by the defendant No.12 that plaintiff who is the wife of Chikkathimma and her son by name Nagaraju, in light of factual matrix stated above, subsequent to the purchase of properties,
although it was legal and valid, are making false claim.
Therefore, the defendant No.12 has contended that the suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed with cost.

5) By considering pleadings and documents produced by the parties, my learned predecessor in offi ce had framed the following issues :-
1.
Whether plaintiff proves that she is the absolute owner in actual possession and enjoyment of suit schedule-A property?

2. Whether plaintiff proves that the order bearing No.RRT/CR/507/2008-09 dated 13.02.2009 ad MR.No.42/2008-09 dated 27.02.2009 did not confer any right, title,
interest or possession or any claim in favour of Munirama S/o Thimma and Muniraju S/o Thimma in respect of the suit schedule B and C property?
3.

Whether plaintiff proves that the fraudulent survey sketch phodi work and akarbandh and also order in MR.No.7/2009-10 dated 05.12.2009 and MR.No.8/2009-10 dated 09.02.2010 did not confer any right, title, interest of possession or any claim in favour of defendants in respect of suit schedule B and C properties?

4. Whether plaintiff proves that the Sale Deed dated 24.09.2011 registered as document No.BMH- 1-05720/2011-12, book No.1, stored in CD No.BMHD515 dated 28.09.2011, in the offi ce of the sub-registrar, Bommanahalli, Bengaluru executed by defendants 1 to 11 and their respective children in favour of proposed defendant No.12 in respect of B and C schedule properties is null and void and not binding on the plaintiff?
5. Whether plaintiff proves her lawful possession over the suit schedule-A property?
6. Whether defendants 1 to 11 prove that valuation of the suit made by plaintiff the plaintiff ins not correct and same is improper and plaintiff has to pay the court fee on the present market value of the suit schedule property as alleged in para-23 of the written statement?
(treated as preliminary issue)
7. Whether defendant No.12 proves that the suit is barred by limitation as alleged in para-2a of the written statement?

9) This suit being one for declaration of title over suit 'A' schedule property the plaintiff has to establish her right, title and interest over the suit property independently.
Failure of defendants to lead evidence, cross -examine the witness does not automatically prove that plaintiff is owner in possession of the suit 'A' schedule property.
The plaintiff is required to prove her title & possession by adducing independent evidence.
In order to show that plaintiff is the owner of 00-16-00 of land in Sy.No.5/1 of Singasandra Village.
The plaintiff has produced grant order dated 27.11.1978 at Ex.P.22.

Therefore, in my considered opinion if any Sale Deed is executed in respect of the land which is remaining in Sy.No.5/1, the plaintiff is not having right to claim the property and challenge the Sale Deed.
Therefore, Sale Deed dated 24.09.2011 cannot said to be null and void when plaintiff has failed to show that property sold under Sale Deed was belonging to her.
As per plaint the suit property is valued for the relief of declaration under Section 24(b) read with Section 7(2)
(a) of KCF and SV Act.
The defendant No.12 has purchased the property as per Sale Deed dated 24.09.2011.
This suit was filed in the year 2010 only after entry of name of Munirama and Muniraju thereafter their descendants.
The entry of name is challenged and relief of declaration is based upon the denial of title and hence, it cannot be said that when denial of title is in the year 2009-10 & suit is filed in the year 2010, relief is barred by limitation.
Therefore, it cannot be said that suit is barred by limitation.
The defendants were in possession of the remaining area in 22 guntas and they have sold the property to defendant No.12 and therefore, plaintiff ought to have asked for possession 1  guntas of land from defendant No.12.
When plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property and relief claimed is perpetual injunction, suit is not maintainable.
The plaintiff is guilty of not seeking appropriate reliefs of possession and hence, issue NO.9 is required to be answered partly in affi rmative holding that suit is bad for not seeking the relief of possession.
The plaintiffs have failed to show that they are in possession & enjoyment of the suit 'A'
schedule property, hence question of granting the relief of perpetual injunction does not arise for consideration.
Plaintiff has sought for declaration to declare that survey settlement and mutations in accordance with survey settlement are null & void and in view of bar under Karnataka Land Revenue Act relief of declaration regarding validity of survey settlement cannot be granted.
The Sale Deed executed by defendant No.1 to 11 in respect of 'B' and 'C' schedule properties is not with respect to schedule 'A' and as such, plaintiff has got no right to challenge the same.
